descriptionChirho: A lifeless human body, a fallen corpse. All three clusters represent the same lexical meaning — a dead body — distinguished only by grammatical number (singular vs. plural) and case (nominative, accusative). Multilingual evidence is uniformly convergent: Spanish 'cadáver' / 'cadáveres,' Hindi 'लाश' / 'लाशों' (corpse/corpses), Arabic 'جُثَّةَ' / 'جُثَثَهُم' (corpse/their corpses), Korean '시체' / '시체들을' (corpse/corpses), Swahili 'maiti' / 'mwili' (dead body/body). The etymological root πίπτω (to fall) is reflected in the sense of a body that has fallen in death.
